algorithms.name: 1. OLS & Maximum Likelihood Estimation
algorithms.subtitle: Ordinary Least Squares via Closed-Form Normal Equations
algorithms.theory: Ordinary Least Squares solves for the optimal weight vector beta by minimizing the sum of squared residual errors. Under Gaussian noise assumptions, OLS is equivalent to the Maximum Likelihood Estimator (MLE), assuming a linear relationship between input continuous audio features (Valence, Energy, Danceability) and target track popularity.
algorithms.caption: Comparison of OLS linear fit vs. Robust Huber regression fit over standardized Valence feature vector.

algorithms.name: 2. Robust Linear Regression (Huber Loss)
algorithms.subtitle: M-Estimators & Outlier-Resistant Cost Surfaces
algorithms.theory: Standard OLS is vulnerable to extreme popularity outliers and viral spikes. Robust Linear Regression uses Huber loss, which behaves quadratically for small residual errors and linearly for large errors (controlled by delta = 1.35), preventing extreme outlier tracks from distorting the global gradient.
algorithms.caption: Robust Huber loss fitting trajectory demonstrating resilience against extreme popularity outliers.

algorithms.name: 3. Ridge Regression (L2 Shrinkage)
algorithms.subtitle: Tikhonov Regularization & Coefficient Paths
algorithms.theory: Ridge regression imposes an L2 penalty on the feature weight vector beta to prevent multicollinearity and overfitting. As lambda increases from 0.1 to 10000, feature weights (Valence, Energy, Danceability) contract smoothly toward zero without exact feature elimination.
algorithms.caption: L2 regularization shrinkage path across 100 logarithmic lambda values from 0.1 to 10,000.

algorithms.name: 4. Bayesian Linear Regression
algorithms.subtitle: Conjugate Gaussian Posterior & Predictive Uncertainty
algorithms.equation: p(w|X,y) = \mathcal{N}(w \mid m_N, S_N), \quad S_N^{-1} = \alpha I + \beta X^T X
algorithms.theory: Bayesian linear regression computes a full probability distribution over weight parameters w rather than a point estimate. Using an isotropic Gaussian prior over w and noise variance alpha/beta, we obtain analytic predictive distributions with explicit 2-sigma confidence bounds.
algorithms.caption: Bayesian predictive mean and ±2 Std Dev uncertainty envelope across the standardized Valence domain.

algorithms.name: 5. Fisher's Linear Discriminant
algorithms.subtitle: Maximized Between-Class vs Within-Class Variance
algorithms.theory: Fisher's Linear Discriminant seeks a 1D projection axis w that maximizes the distance between class centroids (Pop vs. EDM) while minimizing the within-class scatter matrix S_W. It provides optimal linear spatial separation for low-dimensional decision boundaries.
algorithms.caption: 1D Fisher projection density distributions separating Pop and EDM genre clusters.

algorithms.name: 6. Gaussian Discriminant Analysis (GDA)
algorithms.subtitle: Probabilistic Generative Models & Quadratic Boundaries
algorithms.theory: GDA models the class-conditional density p(x|y=k) of features using multivariate Gaussian distributions for each genre class. Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA) allows distinct covariance matrices Sigma_k per class, generating parabolic and hyperbolic decision boundaries.
algorithms.caption: 2D Gaussian feature space ellipses and quadratic decision boundary between Pop and EDM tracks.

algorithms.name: 7. Logistic Regression
algorithms.subtitle: Probabilistic Discriminative Modeling & Sigmoidal Gates
algorithms.equation: p(y=1|x) = \sigma(w^T x + b) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-(w^T x + b)}}
algorithms.theory: Logistic Regression directly models the posterior probability p(y=1|x) using a sigmoid activation function. Optimization via gradient ascent on the log-likelihood function yields robust probability estimates for track popularity hits (Popularity >= 60).
algorithms.caption: Sigmoidal posterior probability curve P(Hit = 1) plotted against standardized Valence.

algorithms.name: 8. Bayesian Logistic Regression
algorithms.subtitle: Intractable Posteriors & Sampling Approximations
algorithms.equation: p(w|D) = \frac{p(w) \prod_{i=1}^N \sigma(y_i w^T x_i)}{\int p(w) \prod_{i=1}^N \sigma(y_i w^T x_i) dw}
algorithms.theory: Unlike linear regression, the logistic likelihood function cannot be analytically integrated with a Gaussian prior due to the non-linear sigmoid gate. Bayesian logistic regression requires approximation strategies (e.g. MCMC sampling or Laplace approximation) to infer parameter posteriors.
algorithms.caption: Posterior distribution over logistic decision thresholds evaluated via Bayesian sampling.

algorithms.name: 9. Laplace Approximation
algorithms.subtitle: Local Quadratic Expansion at MAP Mode
algorithms.theory: The Laplace approximation constructs a Gaussian proxy q(w) for an intractable posterior centered at the Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) mode. The covariance matrix S_N is computed from the inverse Hessian matrix of negative log-posterior at w_MAP.
algorithms.caption: Laplacian Gaussian proxy centered at the MAP vector for non-linear sigmoidal probabilities.

algorithms.name: 10. Support Vector Machines (Linear SVM)
algorithms.subtitle: Max-Margin Hyperplanes & Support Vector Geometry
algorithms.theory: Linear Support Vector Machines optimize a maximum-margin hyperplane separating classes in feature space. Hard margin constraints force zero classification error on support vectors, while soft margin slack variables xi_i allow controlled overlap tuned by hyperparameter C.
algorithms.caption: Linear SVM decision boundary and parallel margin bounds in 2D audio feature space.

algorithms.name: 11. Kernel Functions & RBF Kernel Trick
algorithms.subtitle: Infinite-Dimensional Dual Representation
algorithms.equation: K(x, x') = \exp(-\gamma ||x - x'||^2), \quad f(x) = \sum_{i=1}^N \alpha_i y_i K(x_i, x) + b
algorithms.theory: The Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel trick projects input feature vectors into an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space where non-linear genre clusters become linearly separable. Kernel evaluation K(x, x') computes inner products directly without explicit feature expansion.
algorithms.caption: RBF Kernel non-linear decision boundary isolating non-convex genre clusters.

algorithms.name: 12. Kernelized GLMs (Kernel Ridge Regression)
algorithms.subtitle: Dual Formulation for Non-Linear Continuous Surfaces
algorithms.theory: Kernel Ridge Regression combines Ridge L2 regularization with the kernel trick to solve non-linear regression problems in dual space. Dual weights alpha replace primal weights beta, producing smooth continuous prediction surfaces over non-linear audio trajectories.
algorithms.caption: Kernel Ridge Regression non-linear curve fit capturing continuous non-monotonic track popularity trends.
